thread_text:
Samira Khan: Quick post-all-hands note 12K runtime Q&A follow-up. I had three micro-asks: kernel rollout granularity, batching microburst handling, and a question about KV prefetch heuristics. Dumping here so we can assign.

Priya Desai: I can take kernel + KV prefetch. Maya can confirm schedule and Luis can chime on batching microbursts.

Samira Khan: 1) Kernel rollout: are we doing kernel-v4.2 as a patch on top of v4 or a separate binary? Customers want explicit migration steps.

Priya Desai: kernel-v4.2 is a separate binary but fully compatible at the RPC level. Migration plan: opt-in channel -> per-tenant canaries -> region canaries -> global opt-in. We keep previous binaries for 120 days and provide a single-click rollback per-cluster in Console. No forced flips.

Maya Torres: Schedule note: initial non-prod canaries start 2026-05-18, tenant canaries week of 2026-06-01, region canaries mid-June, global default flip earliest 2026-07-20 pending metrics. Will add to Releases in Console. :spiral_calendar: 

Samira Khan: 2) Batching: We saw tail spikes during microbursts when adaptive widening kicked in. Any guardrails?

Luis Ortega: For microburst protection we9re adding a short-window controller: max_widen_ms and a queue-depth hysteresis. Defaults: max_widen_ms=30, base_window_ms=12, burst_guard=true. adaptive only widens after sustained queue depth > threshold for 3 consecutive measurement windows. Also add p99 cap enforcement via token-shedder so adaptive cannot push p99 above route cap.

Katie Huang: Will Console presets expose these? Product wants simple names: low-latency / balanced / cost.

Luis Ortega: Yes presets map: low-latency -> base_window_ms=8, balanced -> 12, cost -> 40. We9ll show advanced knobs for max_widen_ms and hysteresis if you toggle "advanced batching".

Samira Khan: 3) KV prefetch: customers report cold prefixes when traffic pattern flips. Are we doing heat-based prefetch vs time-based TTL?

Priya Desai: Moving to a hybrid heat-score prefetch. Heat-score = (seen_prefix_hits * recency_factor) / size_cost. Prefetch kicks when heat_score > 0.7 and available memory quota exists. We9ll surface `heat_threshold` and `retain_bytes` in per-route config. Example: `heat_threshold:0.7, retain_bytes:25600000`. Also have `pin_on_first_hit=true` option for conversational sessions that want guaranteed prefix retention.

Samira Khan: Nice. Any telemetry customers can watch to confirm prefetch is working?

Priya Desai: Console will show cache-hit-rate, pinned-count, heat-score distribution, and a small "prefetch-log" stream for canary tenants. We9ll also add an opt-in eval that replays a small set of customer prompts to detect prefix warmness.

Maya Torres: Ops hooks: we9re adding tenant-level webhook for canary-fail and cache-pressure events. ETA: webhooks in Console by 2026-05-10.

deploy-bot: Canary kickoff: kernel-v4.2-canary started on cluster eu-central-1, job=8851.

Samira Khan: Action items: Priya to publish KV heat-score docs + example config, Luis to publish microburst adaptive docs and presets, Maya to add the rollout dates to Releases and enable canary webhooks, Katie to draft a customer-facing note on what to expect during canaries. I9ll collate and add to the all-hands recap.

Priya Desai: I9ll open the docs PR today with YAML snippets and a short explanation of `pin_on_first_hit`.

Luis Ortega: I9ll put the adaptive microburst graphs and threshold recommendations into a short note.

Maya Torres: Will post the timeline and a short rollback playbook in Releases.

Samira Khan: Thanks all. If anyone wants separate tickets for each action please say so and I9ll split. :thumbsup:
